stance.label: Chip bounce fades · Taiwan to open lower · Stay on plan

headline: SOX drops 7.88%, erasing the Huang rally; Taiwan night futures fall 1,842 points, below the bear line
summary: Much of Taiwan's record gain yesterday will likely be given back at today's open: the SOX erased most of its bounce and night futures broke the bear-market line. This is a news-driven bounce fading under tariff and rate-hike pressure, not a credit problem; by the rules US stocks are still in a pullback. Keep regular investing on plan. Today, watch whether the TAIEX holds 39,858 and whether foreign investors sell for an 8th day.

watch.label: TAIEX bear-market line (−20% from peak)
watch.note: Closed 40,122.35 on 11/24; night futures at 38,482 are already below. A close below puts it back in a bear market

watch.label: QQQ tier 4 (−20% from peak)
watch.note: Closed 638.10 on 11/24, 4.8% away; the nearest add tier among the nine

watch.label: S&P 500 200-day line
watch.note: Closed 7,201.09 on 11/24, 2.0% below for 6 days; only a flat 200-day line would mean weak

overview.lead: US stocks gave back most of the chip bounce last night, but money rotated into defensives and the Dow closed higher. Taiwan faces a pullback in tech today, not a broad crash.
points: The SOX fell 7.88% after gaining about 14% the day before.
The Dow rose 0.85% while the Nasdaq fell 1.48%: a rotation, not a broad selloff.
Nvidia (NVDA) fell 5.86% and AMD (AMD) 8.86%; memory stocks fell nearly 10%.
TSMC ADR (TSM) fell 3.96%; Taiwan night futures fell 1,842 points.
By the rules US stocks are still a "pullback in an uptrend," with 1 systemic light on.

focus.lead: The nine tracked names split last night: chip-heavy QQQ and AB International Technology took the biggest hit, and the three Taiwan-linked names will give back yesterday's limit-up gains today.
points: QQQ fell 1.99% and is now 4.8% from tier 4, the nearest add tier.
SPY fell only 0.49%, 7.7% below its peak.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) NAV rose 8.7% on 11/24 and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) 7.8%; today's lower open is not in yet.
The two Taiwan tech funds share 6 top-10 holdings, about 27% by weight, so the pullback will hit both.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) and AB American Growth (LU0683600562) NAVs run only to 11/23 and do not reflect last night's chip drop.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV is still at 11/20.

position.lead: By the framework, nothing new triggered last night; the closest is QQQ tier 4, less than 5% away.
points: QQQ has used 45% of its reserve; tier 4 is 4.8% away.
SPY has used 25% of its reserve; tier 3 is 7.9% away.
0050 has used 70% of its reserve; tier 5 is 14.8% away.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan tier 5 is 6.7% away (11/20 NAV); Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) is 9.3% away (11/24).
AB American Growth tier 3 is 8.5% away (11/23 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend and AB International Technology have used all tiers.

macro.lead: Rates and trade are both pushing down: a December hike is nearly certain, and the US is preparing tariffs on 16 economies including Taiwan.
points: The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.91% and the 2-year 4.63%.
Futures put the odds of a 25 bp December hike at about 95%.
The US Section 301 probe covers Taiwan; findings could come as soon as 11/25, with rates and scope not set.
November consumer confidence jumped to 103.3; the economy does not support a recession story.
High-yield spread is 3.63% (11/23), up 0.25 points in a month, far from the alarm.

sentiment.lead: Fear has not eased: the Fear & Greed Index is still in extreme fear, and short-dated volatility is above long-dated, so traders are still paying for near-term protection.
points: CNN Fear & Greed is 17.4, versus about 26 a week ago.
VIX is 26.36, above its long-run median of 17.6.
9-day VIX at 26.68 is above 3-month VIX at 25.47: the curve is inverted.
Only 15% of Taiwan stocks are above their 200-day line; breadth is still low.

sectors.lead: A classic rotation day in the US: chips and tech fell hard while healthcare, staples and real estate held the market up.
points: Semiconductor ETF (SMH) fell 7.26% and tech fell 3.26%.
Healthcare rose 2.95% and consumer staples 1.66%.
Equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP) rose 0.54% and has beaten cap-weight by 2.7 points over three months.
Software was flat; the selling was concentrated in chips and memory.

taiwan.lead: Taiwan will likely give back a large part of yesterday's gain at the open; the key is whether the close holds the bear-market line. Foreign investors have sold 7 days in a row, so flows cannot support the bounce.
points: Night futures closed at 38,482, below the 39,858 bear-market line.
TSMC ADR closed at US$349.2, about a 3.2% premium to Taiwan shares.
Foreign investors sold NT$50.4B on 11/24, a 7th straight day of net selling.
Foreign net short in TAIEX futures is 103,000 contracts, up about 5,300 in five days.
USD/TWD is 32.955 (11/23); pressure from foreign outflows remains.
The FSC's conditional short-sale curbs are still in place; they slow the drop but cannot stop foreign selling of shares.

watch.lead: Three things to watch next: whether Taiwan holds the bear-market line, whether tonight's PCE firms up rate-hike bets, and the tariff rates on the list.
points: TAIEX 39,858 is today's dividing line at the close.
US PCE inflation and Q3 GDP on the evening of 11/25.
US Section 301 tariff findings as soon as 11/25; Taiwan is on the list.
Dell (DELL) results and guidance beat expectations; AI server demand is not the problem.
US markets close 11/26 for Thanksgiving and close early on 11/27.
Jensen Huang faces a closed-door House hearing on 12/1, the next hurdle for Nvidia.

regime.lead: By the rules, US stocks are still in a pullback and Taiwan is a "pullback with rising risk"; but Taiwan will likely fall back below the bear line today, which would flip it back to bear market.
points: Trend: the S&P 500 is 2.0% below its 200-day line for 6 days, but the line is still rising, so the defense rule has not triggered.
Systemic lights: 1 on for the US (below the 200-day line); 2 for Taiwan, adding broken breadth.
Credit, the economy and financial conditions are fine; the closest light, the high-yield spread, is up 0.25 in a month against a 0.75 threshold.
Capitulation signals: 2 on in the US (extreme fear, inverted volatility), 2 in Taiwan (margin debt down 27.3% in 20 days, breadth washout).
When Taiwan fell this far before, it always went past −20%: all 10 episodes since 2000.
Only 4 were as fast as this one, too few to rely on; 2 of them went past −30%.
US drops to this level mostly stopped in the low teens: only 19 of 103 went past −20%.
What would change this view: a TAIEX close below 39,858 puts it back in a bear market.
5 S&P 500 closes below 7,351 with a flat 200-day line → weak.

news.title: SOX fell 7.88% to 8,832.50; TSMC ADR fell 3.96%; Taiwan night futures fell 1,842 points to 38,482
news.read: Night futures are below the 39,858 bear line; much of yesterday's limit-up rally will likely be given back today, hitting 0050 and the two Taiwan tech funds first.

news.title: Nvidia gave back part of its 31% jump, falling about 6%; Micron and SK Hynix fell nearly 10%, Arm 8%
news.read: Selling hit the chip and memory names that rose most the day before; the Huang-return rally lasted one day.

news.title: Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70; S&P 500 fell 0.50%, Nasdaq 1.48%; odds of a 25 bp December hike about 95%
news.read: Money moved from tech into defensives and old economy, so the index did not break; rate-hike bets are another weight on growth stocks.

news.title: Dell Q3 revenue of US$54.94B beat estimates; AI server revenue US$22B, up 291%; full-year AI server forecast raised to US$78B
news.read: AI server demand is still growing; this chip drop is about flows and headlines, not weaker demand. Supportive for Taiwan's server supply chain.

news.title: US Section 301 overcapacity probe covers 16 economies including Taiwan; new tariffs could come as soon as 11/25, rates and scope not set
news.read: Taiwan, Japan and South Korea are all on the list, and semiconductors are among the sectors probed; until rates are out, it is a risk for Taiwan and Japan stocks.

news.title: US November consumer confidence jumped 11.4 points to 103.3, the highest since January 2025
news.read: Strong consumers keep the recession light off, but also give the Fed more reason to hike.

news.title: FSC conditional short-sale curbs from 11/20: stocks closing down 3.5% or more cannot be shorted below the prior close the next day
news.read: The curbs remain and limit short selling; when they are lifted can be read as a sign markets are back to normal.
